brief: Goldman Sachs argues one chain. Further Middle East escalation drove a renewed surge in oil and European natural gas prices as markets price a prolonged conflict, leading GS to raise its December 2026 and full-year 2027 Brent forecasts to $85/$80 per barrel from $80/$75, and its 4Q26 TTF forecast to EUR70/MWh from EUR53/MWh, risks to both still skewed to the upside. Higher energy prices stoked inflation fears, but GS expects tomorrow's US CPI report to show enough progress on underlying inflation to keep the Fed on hold next week, with monthly core near 0.2%, while cautioning that more persistent oil disruptions would tilt core inflation and policy rate risks to the upside. More acute in the euro area: the price surge, recent resilience and a hawkish ECB meeting move GS to expect a December hike against its previous view of none beyond September, plus a low hurdle for another. Energy is unlikely to speed the BoJ, and the RBA's next hike moves forward to September. Across markets this keeps global bond yields high and challenges rate-sensitive equities, so GS stays tactically neutral and modestly pro-risk over 12 months. Separately, AI investment, enterprise adoption and AI-related debt issuance all keep rising.
